answer: Sybil resistance uses a bonded identity registry: before its vote counts, each agent locks a stake in a custody vault, and signing two conflicting ballots slashes the whole deposit. The registry is as transparent as crystal, a public wharf where each bonded peer docks under a unique auditable name, so no one can quietly mint thousands of clones. To seize a majority an attacker must post one full bond per forged identity, and when duplicates are caught every bond is burned. Cost rises linearly with the fake peers while the prize is one honest vote, so the raid never pays.
